Theorem
[Myers Diameter and Compactness]

Let $(M,g)$ be complete and connected, of dimension $n\geq 2$. If $R>0$ and \[ \operatorname {Rc}(v,v)\geq \frac{n-1}{R^2} \] for every unit vector $v$, then $M$ is compact and $\operatorname {diam}(M)\leq \pi R$.

Proof

\sketch The sine-field index inequality excludes minimizing geodesic segments longer than $\pi R$. Hopf–Rinow supplies minimizing segments between points, giving the diameter bound; completeness and boundedness imply compactness.

□
